reviews.comment: Does not post any extra practice or work to help understand the class for the exams. You get five homework assignments and two exams. His lectures are fine but he does not post a recording or any content on canvas if you had to miss a lecture or go back to review. So, if you miss a part of the lecture there is not a good way to know what he taught.

Tarar is a nice guy, but not a good prof. His lectures are long and tedious, and do not go into much detail that is not in the reading. There are only 4 grades. He gives 3 exams over what he says in class, and a final paper that is completely subjective, with no rubric. Interesting topic, go to class, but be prepared for a boring prof.

3 exams 1 paper 25% each. Received my first ever B on a paper in this class lol. He is not a bad professor by any means, but if you're not particularly interested in international conflict I would not recommend taking. Depressing material especially on top of two other upper-level POLS classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First, the class is only graded by three exams from the little things he mentions in the lecture. Office hours were a waste of time. Exams were not curved with averages around 75-79. He did curve final grades but not everyone's and doesn't answer emails. Sent seven emails and never received an answer. Easy to pass, not recommended as an A blow-off.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was super easy as long as you attend every lecture. Only 3 tests contributed to my grade, but apparently he used to do a final paper in past semesters. The tests are almost always directly from the lecture AND THINGS HE SAYS that may not be on the power point. Go to every lecture and study ~3 days in advance and you'll be fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tarar explained things pretty well, & exams were similar to the homeworks. I didn't have a problem with communication- I emailed him and heard back from him the same day. The lectures were dry but I could zone out for half of class and still follow what was going on. The final was hard, but I still got an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tarar is smart and is good at explaining concepts. Personally, I struggled to follow him during lectures because he has a very monotone voice. Class material isn't difficult per se, but if you miss a class you quickly get behind. Also he does not post grades on Canvas and you have to meet with him after class or during office hours to get grades.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Impossible class. Doesn't grade, doesn't respond to emails, doesn't hold office hours. You have to rely on one person who already knows how to do game theory being in your class.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I did well in the class but it was apparent that his effort was not in the class. Many students as well as I experienced long delays in him answering emails. Grading also took longer than the standard 1 week turnaround. However, based on his class videos I was able to successfully master the material, so I'm torn on a rating to give him.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He did not at all seem prepared to teach this class. Not to mention 308 is probably one of the hardest POLS classes you have to take at A&M. Easily one of the worst professors I have had as far as teaching goes you have 4 HW and 2 tests so you do not have room for error.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Your grade is based on 3 exams and 1 research paper, each worth 25%. Go to every class and take notes. I never read the assigned book or any of the assigned readings because he went over everything in class. So, if you skip, make sure to get the notes from someone. Study your notes thoroughly and you'll do well.
reviews.ratingTags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Tarar gives a lecture every class over an article or book. You just have to show up and take notes over what he says; no outside work. Whatever you take notes over will be on the tests, which are very fair (not difficult). I found the lectures interesting because the subject is interesting. Attendance is not mandatory, but necessary to do well.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bring your pillow to class because he is extremely boring. 3 tests and one paper all 25%, not hard but going to this class is the worst part of my week because of how boring it is.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He WILL put you to sleep. However, he is a great man. Approachable. His international relations class was not very demanding, however it is decently reading dense. Easy test. 3 test of about 10 short answer questions. You should be able to make an A.
Tarar is a very friendly, helpful professor. He has a few quirks as an individual, but that makes him all the better teacher.
